recommendations.regimenLabel: Diagnosis-led — no empirical drug therapy before histology
steps: Structured work-up: examination, bloods, imaging (CT) and targeted tissue diagnosis (excision/core biopsy).
Avoid empirical steroids before histology (can obscure lymphoma diagnosis).
Refer to the appropriate oncology/haematology MDT promptly.
Definitive treatment is tumour-specific after staging.
Manage symptoms and oncological emergencies (hypercalcaemia, SVCO, cord compression).

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Approach to the Patient with Cancer / Lymphoma
Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Oncologic Emergencies
ESMO Clinical Practice Guidelines — Diagnosis and staging of malignancy of unknown primary/lymphoma

drugRefs.dose: 3–4 L over 24 h (titrated to volume status)
drugRefs.why: First step in hypercalcaemia of malignancy — restores volume and promotes calciuresis before a bisphosphonate.
Definitive treatment of hypercalcaemia of malignancy after rehydration; dose-adjust for renal function.
For malignant spinal cord compression to reduce oedema — but withhold before biopsy where lymphoma is suspected, as steroids obscure histology.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Oncologic Emergencies

decision.label: Urgent tissue diagnosis; avoid empirical steroids

confirm: Constitutional 'B' symptoms (weight loss, fevers, night sweats) ± lymphadenopathy/organomegaly suggesting lymphoma/occult malignancy.
